## Current adoption, 11 November 2026

[#297](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/297) adopts the #255 wide-start primary (`f8f64820…`) on Engine `391dfe5d…`, wheel `0962e21d…`. The [adoption account](../results/adoption-297/README.md) owns the fresh replays, finite stability searches, group rules, conditional information and current numerical package. Observation cost is 148.510545654; the same-wheel outgoing reference costs 148.883260440. Normal default replays cover 153 quantities and all 307 declared observations. This is numerical verification and calibration-quality comparison, not new independent physical validation. MDEA #298, manuscript #259 and delivered review remain separate.

The table and linked rows below use the #297 adoption package; earlier studies retain their original parameter and Engine identities.



Current comparison for the #255 record adopted on 11 November 2026 under #297: `f8f64820…`, MEA association volume 0.036305439. Its exact parameter identity is linked from the [overview](../notebook.qmd#working-record).

# Question

How well does the adopted #255 record reproduce the retained high-temperature CO₂ pressures?

# Result

The adopted #255 record predicts the 54 canonical 100–120 °C pressures with 23.67% AARD, ranging from 19.43% (Mamun 2005, 120 °C) to 30.90% (Jou 1995, 120 °C). These are non-fitted predictions and do not qualify high-temperature process use.

# Basis and method

Average absolute relative deviation (AARD) is computed within each named retained cohort; source, temperature, pressure basis and row availability remain in the source-state assessment.

# Limits and evidence type

These are non-fitted comparisons at the retained source states. Data-access history and overlapping membership limit an independent-prediction interpretation. No matched no-heat calculation was made.
